The fixed costs have been estimated based on maintenance costs, manpower costs, property tax, insurance, etc. Task 6.0 Final Report Submission Subtask 6.1 Initial Engineering Design & Cost Estimate Based on Tasks 2.0 (including the TEA prepared as part of the task) and 3.0, the initial engineering design and cost estimate (Attachment 7) have been prepared. Subtask 6.2 Techno-Economic Analysis The Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) was prepared based on the methodology given in Appendix C of this SOPO. The TEA (Attachment 8) includes general process flow diagrams of all major process equipment, material and energy balances, complete stream tables, and economic analyses (capital, operating, and maintenance costs). Subtask 6.3 Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) Risk Assessment Dastur prepared an EH&S risk assessment and mitigation plan (Attachment 9) to assess the proposed project's environmental friendliness, impact, and safety. Guidelines have been provided in the EH&S Assessment for handling project-generated wastes and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous wastes, following all applicable Federal, state, and local regulations and waste management plans. 4.0 Proposed Carbon Capture System The proposed carbon capture scheme envisaged at Burns Harbor is depicted in Figure 1. The available BF gas (Stream 1) is tapped from the BF header and undergoes a compositional shift by passing it through a series of Water Gas Shift (WGS) Reactors, which converts ~80% of the carbon monoxide (CO) in the BF gas to CO (Stream 2). The increase in CO content (22% in BF gas vs. 32% after the WGS unit) 2 2 in the shifted gas enables the capture of up to 85% of CO e in the available BF gas, with benefits of 2 lower capture island footprint, single train, lower CAPEX and easier fit within the space-constrained Burns Harbor plant. The post-capture H -rich fuel gas (H RF or Stream 3) is sent to the existing 2 2 powerhouse to produce captive power for in-plant use; the use of the H -rich fuel gas instead of the BF 2 gas (present scenario) in the powerhouse does not require any modification to the existing burners, thus minimizing disruptions to existing operations.
